text:
The World Bank Group approved $1.06 billion in loans to help decarbonise Brazil’s high-value-added and energy-intensive industries, with the operation expected to mobilise a further $1.8 bln in development and commercial financing, it announced on Tuesday.

Developed in partnership with the National Bank for Economic and Social Development (BNDES), the initiative targets key sectors across industrial and energy value chains that are also highly emissions-intensive, including steel, cement, chemicals, and aluminium, as well as low-carbon fuels.

The goal is to accelerate the deployment of new technologies in these sectors, crowd in private sector financing, and position Brazil as a global reference for industrial transformation, according to the World Bank.

Resources will come from two loans: $1 bln from the International Bank for Reconstruction and Development (IBRD) and $60 million from the Clean Technology Fund.

The initiative is expected demonstrate the commercial viability of low-carbon industrial investments, proponents said.

It also aims to reduce the risks of early investments and mobilise private capital as green industrial markets develop, helping Brazil meet its goal of cutting the GHG intensity of industrial GDP by 30% by 2033.

“Brazil’s clean energy matrix is one of its greatest competitive advantages. This project is about turning that advantage into a driver of industrial transformation, one that reduces emissions, attracts investment, and creates quality jobs in the industries of tomorrow,” said Cecile Fruman, World Bank director for Brazil.

The financing will focus on three interconnected areas of Brazil’s industrial decarbonisation:

Low-carbon industrial commodities: Funding will help cement, steel, glass, chemicals, and aluminium producers cut emissions while maintaining their competitiveness in global markets

Low-carbon fuels: Investment will support sustainable aviation fuel (SAF), e-methanol, biomethane, and other emerging fuels aimed at reducing emissions from aviation and maritime transport

Shared infrastructure: Financing will support common-use infrastructure, including storage facilities and pipelines for green hydrogen and ammonia, allowing multiple industries to access low-carbon energy inputs and helping reduce barriers to the adoption of new technologies

“The project is aligned with Brazil’s new industry plan, its Ecological Transformation Plan, the National Fertilizer Plan, and the country’s Paris Agreement commitments. It also illustrates how development finance can help bridge the gap between technological innovation and commercial scale,” said Marcos Vinicius Chiliatto, executive director at the World Bank representing Brazil and other Latin American and Caribbean countries, in a LinkedIn post.

A reduction of around 35 mln tonnes of CO2e is expected through the programme, according to the director, who participated in the operation.

Chiliatto noted that this is the first time in more than 30 years that BNDES has received a loan from the IBRD.

text:
Air Serbia sees sustainable aviation fuel (SAF) as an important element of the aviation industry’s decarbonisation efforts but says its price and limited availability remain major obstacles to wider adoption. Speaking at the OIE Serbia conference, the carrier’s General Manager for Commercial and Strategy, Bosko Rupić, said SAF currently accounts for around 1.7% of the airline’s fuel use, up from approximately 0.67% in 2024. Although Serbia is not a member of the European Union, a significant proportion of Air Serbia’s operations involve EU markets, where regulations are gradually increasing the required share of SAF. Under current targets, the proportion will rise from 2% to 6% by 2030 and eventually reach 70% by 2050. SAF supplies are currently not available at Belgrade Airport.

Mr Rupić noted that SAF is between two and three times more expensive than conventional jet fuel. “Fuel accounts for between 20% and 30% of an airline’s total costs”, Mr Rupić said, adding that carriers generally operate with margins of only 3% to 4%. He argued that the financial burden of aviation’s decarbonisation cannot be placed solely on airlines or passed on entirely to passengers through higher ticket prices. According to Mr Rupić, greater involvement from governments and the wider public sector will be necessary to support the transition and offset some of the additional costs.

Fleet modernisation is another important part of Air Serbia’s efforts to reduce emissions. Mr Rupić pointed to the usage of newer-generation aircraft, including the Airbus A220, through a wet-lease arrangement, which offer lower fuel consumption and consequently reduced carbon emissions. New-generation aircraft can consume between 15% and 20% less fuel than the equipment they replace.

text:
Listen to the audio version of this article (generated by AI).

New Internal Revenue Service (IRS) guidance released last week confirms that gas extracted from livestock manure qualifies for a federal clean fuel tax credit, paving the way for increased investment in biogas projects.

The move comes as farms increasingly turn to anaerobic digestion to deal with massive amounts of manure. Proponents say the tax credits will bolster an industry that provides a solution to excess waste and turns otherwise emitted methane into a usable fuel. Critics, however, say the IRS is rewarding large, polluting farms for a practice that incentivizes packing more animals into already highly concentrated operations.

Anaerobic digesters use bacteria to break down large amounts of manure and turn it into “biogas,” which is a mix of mostly methane and carbon dioxide and can be refined into RNG and used in some vehicles and as a natural gas substitute. There are an estimated 394 manure-based digesters operating in the US, with more than 70 under construction, representing a 55% increase over the past decade.

Such digesters can also break down other farm waste like food scraps and crop residues — sources that were also included in the new guidance. In addition to RNG from manure and farm waste, the credit also pertains to ethanol, biodiesel, hydrogen and sustainable aviation fuel.

Biogas advocates lauded the guidance, saying it provided much needed clarity, will kickstart more biogas investment, and that it supports farmers and rural communities. Such proponents say manure digesters are a climate-win, reducing methane emissions from manure generated at concentrated animal feeding operations (CAFOs) and spread on land as fertilizer.

“With this clarity, there are going to be biogas projects that are developed because there’s lots of organic waste that needs to be recycled,” said Patrick Serfass, executive director of the American Biogas Council. A report from the council in February found massive potential for extracting gas from farm waste — including the potential for more than 11,000 additional systems on farms. The report estimates there are currently 631 biogas capture systems at farms in the US, accounting for 25% of all RNG produced last year.

“With this clarity, there are going to be biogas projects that are developed because there’s lots of organic waste that needs to be recycled.” – Patrick Serfass, American Biogas Council

Serfass said only about 10% to 20% of the organic material from farms is currently recycled.

“There’s just tons, literally millions of tons, of organic waste that need to be recycled. And so the tax credit helps projects that could provide a valuable community service,” he said.

The IRS guidance established emissions rates for renewable natural gas (RNG) produced from animal manure, along with other non-fossil fuels, under the Clean Fuel Production Tax Credit, known as 45Z. The amount of the credit depends on how carbon-intensive the fuel is, based on calculations from a model the US Department of Agriculture (USDA) developed. Since 45Z was passed as part of the Inflation Reduction Act in 2022 biogas producers have been unclear as to whether such projects qualify for the credit.

“Today’s guidance helps America’s farmers, ranchers, and fuel producers access growing opportunities in the domestic biofuels market,” said IRS Chief Executive Officer Frank J. Bisignano in a statement.

Given that the 45Z credits are set to expire in 2029 — and it’s unclear what will become of them beyond that — Serfass said the new guidance will likely spur along biogas “projects that are already in the pipeline, already in development, or ones that can be built quickly.”

However, critics of manure-to-gas projects say such facilities are prone to leaks, incentivize adding more animals to already packed farming operations, and are too reliant on federal and state loans and subsidies. In California, which leads the nation in gas produced from manure digesters, researchers estimate that expansion that takes place at dairy farms that build digesters wipes out an estimated 9% of the farms’ purported greenhouse gas reductions.

Food & Water Watch senior staff attorney Tyler Lobdell said with the new guidance “the IRS is now putting their thumb on the scale in favor of large, industrial, polluting factory farms.”

“The program prioritizes dirty fuels over clean ones,” he said.

“The program prioritizes dirty fuels over clean ones.” -Tyler Lobdell, Food & Water Watch

The clean fuel credit for manure digester gas will be calculated against how the farm previously handled its waste — including open lagoons, deep pits, solid storage and other methods. The IRS said it will provide different carbon intensity rates for different types of manure sometime later this year.

“Since liquid manure storage is among the highest-emitting management methods, comparing against it, rather than an average, is likely going to produce a bigger credit,” said Andrew deCoriolis, executive director of Farm Forward. “Biogas proponents will argue this just makes the accounting more accurate, but good accounting isn’t the same as good policy.”

He added that the credit won’t help smaller, pasture-based operations that never relied on liquid manure storage because there’s no high-emitting baseline for them to be measured against.

The credit “operates as a revenue source for whoever runs the biggest, dirtiest, most liquid-manure-intensive operations, and the tax code doesn’t distinguish ‘a bad actor cleaning up’ from ‘a bad actor being rewarded for having been bad for decades,’” he said.

The Trump administration has sent mixed signals on manure digester biogas since taking office. Last year’s One Big Beautiful Bill Act preserved clean energy status for manure-derived biogas, while stripping away subsidies for solar and wind.

However, the US Department of Agriculture currently has a moratorium on loan guarantees for anaerobic digesters — many of which are issued for manure digesters — through the end of 2026 due to “persistent and escalating concerns” about performance and financial solvency. The New Lede, however, reported that a February loan transfer removed the bulk of USDA digester delinquencies.

When the National Business Aviation Association’s Business Aviation Convention & Exhibition (NBAA-BACE) returns to the Las Vegas Convention Center October 20-22, it will do so against the backdrop of an industry that has changed almost beyond recognition since business aviation first took shape. Phillips 66® Aviation has evolved right alongside it, pioneering advancements in aviation fuel and growing into one of the industry’s most established fuel suppliers.

Phillips 66 Aviation traces its aviation roots back nearly 100 years to Bartlesville, Oklahoma, where it was founded in 1927. The early groundwork would prove consequential. Phillips 66 Aviation pioneered 100-octane avgas that played a role in fueling military aircraft during World War II, and followed it with innovations like anti-icing additives that improved fuel performance and safety in the decades after. The company’s fuel history also found its way into aviation milestones outside of wartime, including some of the earliest long-distance flights between the U.S. mainland and Hawaii. Nearly a century later, Phillips 66 Aviation is still advancing solutions forward with breakthroughs in sustainable aviation fuel for both general and business aviation.

Among the many suppliers serving FBOs and flight departments, Phillips 66 Aviation stands apart. Phillips 66 Aviation is the only company in the industry that both refines and supplies its own aviation fuel. That distinction translates directly into what FBOs and flight departments seek day to day: greater reliability, more consistent supply, and the confidence that comes from working with the source. That expertise, built over nearly a century of refining, is what brings a deeper understanding of aviation fuel from production through delivery, helping customers keep their operations moving with confidence.

It also underpins the company’s ongoing commitment to its branded FBO network. Phillips 66 Aviation’s FBO network has increased to 740 locations across the country, ranging from long-established, family-run operations to newer operations serving today’s aviation community. Each of those FBOs, whatever their size or history, draws from the same refiner-direct supply chain, giving them a reliable supply, strong customer service, and personalized solutions to meet the evolving needs of FBOs.

Nearly a century of experience has shaped how Phillips 66 Aviation refines and delivers fuel, and it’s also shaped how operators access it. The Contract Fuel program takes that same focus on reliability and service and applies it to making fuel purchasing simpler for today’s operators. With discounted fuel pricing nationwide, the program eliminates the fuel cards, fuel releases, or minimum volume requirements operators often navigate with other providers.

The company sums up its century in the business with a simple phrase: “Cleared for Go.” More than a tagline, it reflects the brand’s focus on helping customers keep moving forward. From fuel and service to programs and support, Phillips 66 Aviation works to make every part of the experience ready for what’s next.

NBAA-BACE remains the single largest gathering of decision-makers in business aviation, featuring corporate flight departments, charter operators, FBO chains, and OEMs all converging in one place for three days each October. It’s also where Phillips 66 Aviation is showcasing its offerings to an audience that includes both longtime customers and new customers who are looking at new fuel solutions.

The global shipping and logistics giant has a target toreach carbon neutrality by 2040. FedEx also aims to decrease its aircraft emissions intensity by 40% by 2040, compared to a 2005 baseline.

As it owns a big portion of its transportation assets, FedEx’s scope 1 emissions generate the largest portion of its carbon footprint. About 80% of its scope 1 emissions are from jet fuel use alone, according to its website.

“SAF is one of the most impactful decarbonization solutions available to aviation today and an important part of our approach to reducing emissions,” said FedEx Chief Sustainability Officer and Vice President of Environmental Affairs Karen Blanks Ellis in the Tuesday release. “Expanding our procurement allows us to employ more SAF in our network while bolstering the demand for greater production and scale.”

SAF has the potential to reduce lifecycle carbon emissions by up to 80% compared to conventional fossil kerosene, according to the Air Transport Action Group. However, the International Air Transport Association found that SAF use made up just 0.6% of global jet fuel use in 2025 and is expected to provide only 0.8% of jet fuel consumption this year. Although SAF production doubled last year, its growth is expected to slow this year, according to IATA.

Yusen Logistics and Finnair agree on Sustainable Aviation Fuel (SAF)

Yusen Logistics and Finnair announce an agreement concerning Sustainable Aviation Fuel (SAF)-related environmental attributes. Through this collaboration, the companies aim to support the reduction of lifecycle greenhouse gas emissions associated with air cargo transportation and contribute to efforts to decarbonize global supply chains.

Under the agreement, Yusen Logistics will purchase SAF-related environmental attributes from Finnair. The arrangement uses a Book-and-Claim mechanism, under which the environmental attributes associated with SAF use can be allocated separately from the physical movement of fuel and cargo.

The agreement was concluded with the support of Western Associates, Inc. (WAI), Finnair’s General Sales Agent in Japan.

The initiative forms part of Yusen Logistics’ broader sustainability strategy and supports Finnair’s efforts to expand the use of SAF in aviation.

The companies recognize the importance of collaborative and scalable approaches that address emissions from air cargo transportation while maintaining reliable international logistics services.

The agreement reflects the shared ambition of Yusen Logistics and Finnair to support customers seeking ways to address emissions associated with air freight transportation through SAF-related environmental attributes and to support the aviation industry’s transition toward lower-carbon operations.

The collaboration also demonstrates the importance of partnerships across the logistics ecosystem, bringing together airlines and logistics providers to support demand for SAF and contribute to the aviation industry’s broader decarbonization efforts.

Through this mechanism, customers can support the use of SAF. Participating customers may receive certificates and emissions-related reporting concerning the SAF environmental attributes allocated to them. description:

Sustainable aviation fuel (SAF).

text:
Neste and United Airlines have extended their existing agreement on the supply of sustainable aviation fuel (SAF) blended with conventional jet fuel to flights departing Chicago O’Hare International Airport in the United States and Amsterdam Airport Schiphol in the Netherlands. The extension of the agreement reinforces the long-term, strategic collaboration between Neste and United, highlighting a shared ambition of contributing to greenhouse gas (GHG) emissions reduction from aviation through the deployment of SAF*.

Based on the extended contract, Neste’s SAF deliveries to United at Amsterdam began in June 2026 and continued through August 2026. Deliveries of SAF to Chicago O’Hare from this contract started in July 2026 and are planned to continue until June 2027. According to the agreement, Neste will supply Neste MY Sustainable Aviation Fuel™ blended with conventional jet fuel to United Airlines.

"United was the first airline in the world to fly on blended SAF in regular operations, and we've spent the years since proving it can work at scale in day-to-day flying – including being the first airline to purchase and use blended SAF at Chicago O'Hare. Continuing our work with Neste across two continents reflects a shared conviction that SAF is available and capable of being scalable," said Lauren Riley, Chief Sustainability Officer at United Airlines.

In 2025, United used over 83,000 metric tons (roughly 27.7 million gallons) of SAF, a 104% increase over the prior year, making it the largest SAF user among major U.S. airlines that year, based on publicly available reports, and expanded its SAF use to three additional hub airports in Newark, Washington D.C. and Houston, bringing the airlines’ SAF usage to six out of its seven domestic hubs. At Chicago O’Hare specifically, United was the first airline to purchase and use blended SAF in August 2024. O’Hare is United’s largest hub by daily departures and among the airline’s most important global gateways, making it a key location for scaling the use of blended SAF in day-to-day operations.

In Amsterdam, United has been using Neste MY SAF at Schiphol Airport since 2022. United was the first airline globally to use SAF in ongoing operations. Leveraging SAF and other measures to reduce GHG emissions, United is committed to reaching its net-zero emissions by 2050 goal.

"This extended agreement with United Airlines covering two international airports across two major aviation regions is a testament to our joint belief in the critical role of SAF in reducing aviation related GHG emissions*. By continuing to make SAF available at two of United’s key hubs, we are proving that SAF is a readily available, scalable solution, and we look forward to continuing our longstanding collaboration," says Carl Nyberg, Senior Vice President, Commercial, Renewable Products business at Neste.

Sustainable aviation fuel (SAF). Neste MY Sustainable Aviation Fuel is an alternative to fossil-based jet fuel available today that can help reduce aviation related GHG emissions*. Neste’s SAF is made from renewable raw materials, such as used cooking oil and animal fat waste. SAF is certified for commercial use after blending up to 50% with conventional jet fuel and works seamlessly with existing aircraft engines and fueling infrastructure.

Today, Neste’s global SAF production capability is 1.5 million metric tons (around 515 million gallons) per annum, and it is set to grow to 2.2 million metric tons (around 750 million gallons) in 2027, when the expansion of Neste’s Rotterdam refinery is completed.

*) Neat, i.e. unblended, Neste MY Sustainable Aviation Fuel fulfills the mandatory sustainability criteria, including greenhouse gas emission reduction requirements over its life cycle compared to fossil fuel in accordance with e.g. ReFuelEU, CORSIA or RFS. While SAF and fossil jet fuel release similar amounts of CO2 during flight, SAF’s life cycle climate impact is smaller than fossil jet fuel’s. SAF can currently be blended up to 50% with conventional jet fuel.

description:

text:
Praj Industries and GEVO, Inc. (NASDAQ: GEVO) today announced the signing of a Development & Commercialization Agreement for Bio-Isobutanol (Bio-IBA) technology in India, reinforcing their long-standing association to advance sustainable low-carbon fuel solutions.

Under the agreement, Praj will lead the commercialization of Bio-IBA technology in India, with exclusive rights to deploy the technology in the country. The partnership will focus on developing commercial opportunities for Bio-IBA, with a primary emphasis on diesel blending applications that have the potential to reduce the carbon intensity of one of the world's most widely used transportation and industrial fuels.

The agreement builds upon more than a decade of association between the two companies to adapt, develop and advance Bio-IBA technology for Indian feedstocks and market requirements. Praj's deep understanding of India's sugar- and starch-based feedstocks, its expertise in engineering, project execution, scale-up and market development, combined with Gevo's Bio-IBA technology, will support its scale-up and commercial adoption in India.

In a separate development aligned with the broader objective of advancing Bio-IBA adoption, Praj is currently establishing India's first commercial Bio-IBA demonstration plant for a leading Oil Marketing Company (OMC). The project is being designed, engineered, supplied and erected by Praj based on Gevo's licensed Bio-IBA technology. The demonstration plant is expected to play an important role in validating production, supply-chain and market-development pathways for future commercialization opportunities in India.

Bio-IBA presents a promising opportunity for reducing the carbon footprint of diesel across a wide range of applications, including: transportation, agriculture, mining, construction and industrial operations. Given India's large diesel economy and abundant renewable feedstock resources, Bio-IBA has the potential to become an important component in the country's transition towards lower-carbon fuels. According to Petroleum Planning & Analysis Cell (PPAC), India consumed approximately 94.7 million tonnes (29.7 billion US gallons) of high-speed diesel in FY2025-26.

Encouragingly, stakeholders across the value chain, including fuel producers, vehicle and equipment manufacturers, research institutions and end users, are actively working towards enabling Bio-IBA-based diesel blending in India. Multiple initiatives aimed at technology validation, application development, regulatory assessment and supply-chain preparedness are progressing in parallel, reflecting growing industry interest in bringing diesel blending solutions to commercial reality.

"This agreement marks an important milestone in our relationship with Praj and in the advancement of Bio-IBA in India," said Gevo Chief Executive Officer Paul Bloom. "Gevo brings proven renewable isobutanol technology and commercialization experience, while Praj contributes deep expertise in engineering, deployment and market development. Together, we are creating a framework to unlock new opportunities for Bio-IBA, particularly in diesel applications, while supporting broader decarbonization objectives."

"Our collaboration with Gevo has steadily evolved through technology development, application innovation and market-building efforts over the years," said Dr. Pramod Chaudhari, Founder Chairman, Praj Industries. "This Development & Commercialization Agreement establishes a strong foundation for bringing Bio-IBA to the Indian market. We believe Bio-IBA has the potential to emerge as an important renewable fuel solution for the diesel economy, complementing India's broader energy transition and sustainability goals."

Beyond diesel applications, Bio-IBA also serves as a platform molecule for the production of Sustainable Aviation Fuel (SAF) and other renewable chemicals, further highlighting its versatility and expected long-term strategic importance within the emerging bioeconomy.

About Praj:

Praj Industries Limited is a global biotechnology and engineering company driven by innovation, integration and delivery capabilities. Over the past four decades, Praj has been enabling the transition to a sustainable future through solutions across the Bioeconomy, Energy Transition and Industrial Infrastructure. With over 1,000 customer references in more than 100 countries across six continents, Praj has established itself as a trusted global technology and engineering partner.

Bio-Mobility® and Bio-Prism® are the cornerstones of Praj's contribution to the global Bioeconomy. The Bio-Mobility® platform offers technology solutions for the production of renewable transportation fuels, supporting sustainable decarbonization through a circular bioeconomy. The Bio-Prism® portfolio comprises technologies for renewable chemicals and materials that advance sustainability while reimagining nature.

Praj Matrix, the Company's state-of-the-art research and development centre, drives the development of next-generation technologies for clean energy, renewable fuels, chemicals and materials.

The Company's wholly owned subsidiaries further strengthen its capabilities across high-growth sectors. Praj GenX delivers advanced manufacturing, modular process systems and critical process equipment for industries including oil & gas, advanced biofuels, sustainable aviation fuel (SAF), hydrogen, carbon capture and mission-critical digital infrastructure, including hyperscale data centers. Praj HiPurity Systems provides high-purity process systems and turnkey solutions for the pharmaceutical, biotechnology, healthcare and allied industries.

Praj's diversified portfolio spans Bio-energy solutions, Critical Process Equipment & Modular Systems, High Purity Systems, Industrial Wastewater Treatment, Zero Liquid Discharge (ZLD) solutions, Breweries and emerging engineering solutions for global infrastructure markets. Guided by purpose-driven leadership and a commitment to sustainability, Praj continues to create value for customers, communities and stakeholders worldwide.

Praj Industries Limited is listed on the BSE Limited and the National Stock Exchange of India Limited (NSE).

Gevo is pioneering low-carbon solutions with cost-effective, drop-in fuels that contribute to energy security, abate carbon and strengthen rural communities to drive economic growth. Gevo's innovative technology can be used to make a variety of renewable products, including SAF, motor fuels, chemicals, and other materials. Gevo's business model includes developing, financing, and operating production facilities that create jobs and revitalize communities. Gevo owns and operates an ethanol plant with an adjacent carbon capture and storage (CCS) facility and Class VI carbon-storage well. text:
BATON ROUGE, La. – Louisiana Economic Development announced the second round of Louisiana FastSites, continuing the state’s investment in infrastructure and site improvements that help communities compete for new economic development opportunities.

The Round II application period will open Oct. 1 and close Dec. 1, with $50 million available for eligible projects. Competitive projects must be development-ready and able to begin construction activities within nine months, include matching funds and demonstrate a path to repayment.

“FastSites is changing how Louisiana prepares for economic development by investing before infrastructure becomes a barrier,” LED Chief Economic Competitiveness Officer Ileana Ledet said. “The first round showed the demand from communities ready to move critical site and infrastructure projects forward, and Round II builds on that progress by helping more communities put the infrastructure in place to compete for future projects.”

FastSites is backed by the $200 million Site Investment and Infrastructure Fund established by the Louisiana Legislature to support site development in every corner of the state. The inaugural round advanced projects that expanded development-ready acreage, improved access and utilities, and positioned sites for business expansion and new investment.

The program is designed to reduce the time, risk and cost associated with preparing sites for investment while extending the impact of the state’s dollars. By pairing state funding with local or private investment and requiring a path to repayment, FastSites allows repaid funds to be reinvested in future site development opportunities.

Eligible applicants include economic development organizations, municipalities, redevelopment authorities, political subdivisions and other qualifying entities. Privately owned sites may also be eligible under program requirements.

To help potential applicants learn more about the program and application process, LED will host a webinar on Friday, Sept. 18, at 1 p.m. Registration is available in advance here. After registering, attendees will receive a confirmation email with details about joining the webinar.

For more information about FastSites and application guidelines, visit OpportunityLouisiana.com/FastSites.

title: From biomass to sustainable aviation fuel: Valmet advances green energy collaboration
description:

Zhu Xiangdong represented Valmet at the signing ceremony alongside representatives from One Power and Morimatsu Group.
The project highlights the growing role of biomass-based solutions in the decarbonization of energy and transportation systems.
By bringing together expertise from across the value chain, the initiative seeks to create an integrated pathway from biomass feedstocks to black pellets and ultimately sustainable aviation fuel.

text:
As one of the guest countries of Honor at this year's CIFIT, Finland was represented by a delegation led by Finland's Minister of Economic Affairs, Sakari Puisto. The delegation brought together Finnish companies and institutions to explore new opportunities for economic and technological cooperation between Finland and China.

Advancing industrial transformation through innovation

Representing Valmet, Aki Niemi, Executive Vice President, Global Supply, participated in the event and introduced Valmet’s technology at the China-Finland Economic and Trade Cooperation Exchange Meeting. Under the theme “Advancing Industrial Transformation Towards a Sustainable and Regenerative Future,” he highlighted how Valmet helps customers improve operational efficiency, optimize resource utilization, and accelerate their sustainability ambitions through advanced technologies and lifecycle solutions.

Supporting a major sustainable fuel initiative

A significant milestone during the event was the signing of a Letter of Intent for the Fujian Kemen Port integrated energy project, which aims to combine the production of 1.2 million tons of black pellets with sustainable aviation fuel (SAF) development. Zhu Xiangdong represented Valmet at the signing ceremony alongside representatives from One Power and Morimatsu Group.

The project highlights the growing role of biomass-based solutions in the decarbonization of energy and transportation systems. By bringing together expertise from across the value chain, the initiative seeks to create an integrated pathway from biomass feedstocks to black pellets and ultimately sustainable aviation fuel.

Pretreatment technology enables high-quality black pellet production

At the heart of Valmet's contribution to this development is BioTrac, the company's pretreatment technology designed to upgrade woody biomass and agricultural residues into high-quality black pellets. The process uses medium-pressure saturated steam to modify the biomass structure, followed by rapid pressure release and fiber defibration.

This pretreatment process improves the fuel characteristics of the biomass, increasing its calorific value while enhancing hydrophobicity. After pelletizing, the result is a dense and durable black pellet with improved grindability and fuel performance.

Compared with conventional white pellets, black pellets offer several advantages, including:

Higher energy density

Improved water resistance

Better handling and storage properties

Enhanced suitability for coal replacement and gasification applications

Strong potential as a low-carbon fuel solution

Building partnerships for a sustainable future

Valmet's participation at CIFIT reflects the company's continued commitment to supporting customers and partners in their transition toward more sustainable energy systems. Through technological innovation, strategic partnerships, and renewable fuel solutions, Valmet is helping shape a future where industrial growth and environmental responsibility go hand in hand.

text:
FedEx Expands Sustainable Aviation Fuel Agreements across U.S. Air Network

(FedEx) ... FedEx is scaling its sustainable aviation fuel (SAF) procurement through new agreements projected to secure more than 20 million gallons of neat SAF across five U.S. airports through calendar year 2027.

The agreements span FedEx operations at Newark Liberty International Airport (EWR), Oakland International Airport (OAK), Miami International Airport (MIA), John F. Kennedy International Airport (JFK), and Dallas Fort Worth International Airport (DFW). The agreements are expected to deliver SAF at blend ratios ranging from 30% to 50%, depending on location.

FedEx is working toward its goal to source 30% of jet fuel blended from alternative sources by 2030, while expanding the use of SAF across its U.S. air network. “The latest agreements represent an expansion of SAF within the FedEx air network enabled, in part, by state and federal level incentives,” said Greg Paulus, vice president of Enterprise Sourcing. Starting in 2025, FedEx secured approximately 5 million gallons of neat SAF through agreements that resulted in the deployment of 16.5 million gallons of blended SAF across five U.S. airports. With this next phase of procurement, SAF blends represent a significant share of FedEx jet fuel use at the airports mentioned above.

“SAF is one of the most impactful decarbonization solutions available to aviation today and an important part of our approach to reducing emissions,” said Karen Blanks Ellis, chief sustainability officer and vice president of Environmental Affairs at FedEx. “For the market to grow, supply needs to be reliable, affordable, and sustainable. Expanding our procurement allows us to employ more SAF in our network while bolstering the demand for greater production and scale.”

The new agreements are another step in putting more SAF into use across the FedEx network while demonstrating the demand that exists today. As the SAF market develops, FedEx will continue evaluating opportunities to expand its use where supply, infrastructure, and economics align with the needs of its air network.

Learn more about the FedEx sustainability strategy and the company’s goal of carbon-neutral global operations by 2040 here: https://www.fedex.com/en-us/sustainability/our-approach.html

text:
Neste Corporation, Press Release, 16 September 2026 at 2 p.m. (EET)

Photo: courtesy of United Airlines

Neste and United Airlines extended their existing agreement on the supply of sustainable aviation fuel (SAF) blended with conventional jet fuel to flights departing Chicago O’Hare International Airport in the United States and Amsterdam Airport Schiphol in the Netherlands. The extension of the agreement reinforces the long-term, strategic collaboration between Neste and United, highlighting a shared ambition of contributing to greenhouse gas (GHG) emissions reduction from aviation through the deployment of SAF*.

Based on the extended contract, Neste’s SAF deliveries to United at Amsterdam began in June 2026 and continued through August 2026. Deliveries of SAF to Chicago O’Hare from this contract started in July 2026 and are planned to continue until June 2027. According to the agreement, Neste will supply Neste MY Sustainable Aviation Fuel™ blended with conventional jet fuel to United Airlines.

"United was the first airline in the world to fly on blended SAF in regular operations, and we've spent the years since proving it can work at scale in day-to-day flying – including being the first airline to purchase and use blended SAF at Chicago O'Hare. Continuing our work with Neste across two continents reflects a shared conviction that SAF is available and capable of being scalable," said Lauren Riley, Chief Sustainability Officer at United Airlines.

In 2025, United used over 83,000 metric tons (roughly 27.7 million gallons) of SAF, a 104% increase over the prior year, making it the largest SAF user among major U.S. airlines that year, based on publicly available reports, and expanded its SAF use to three additional hub airports in Newark, Washington D.C. and Houston, bringing the airlines’ SAF usage to six out of its seven domestic hubs. At Chicago O’Hare specifically, United was the first airline to purchase and use blended SAF in August 2024. O’Hare is United’s largest hub by daily departures and among the airline’s most important global gateways, making it a key location for scaling the use of blended SAF in day-to-day operations.

In Amsterdam, United has been using Neste MY SAF at Schiphol Airport since 2022. United was the first airline globally to use SAF in ongoing operations. Leveraging SAF and other measures to reduce GHG emissions, United is committed to reaching its net-zero emissions by 2050 goal.

"This extended agreement with United Airlines covering two international airports across two major aviation regions is a testament to our joint belief in the critical role of SAF in reducing aviation related GHG emissions*. By continuing to make SAF available at two of United’s key hubs, we are proving that SAF is a readily available, scalable solution, and we look forward to continuing our longstanding collaboration," says Carl Nyberg, Senior Vice President, Commercial, Renewable Products business at Neste.

Sustainable aviation fuel (SAF)

Neste MY Sustainable Aviation Fuel is an alternative to fossil-based jet fuel available today that can help reduce aviation related GHG emissions*. Neste’s SAF is made from renewable raw materials, such as used cooking oil and animal fat waste. SAF is certified for commercial use after blending up to 50% with conventional jet fuel and works seamlessly with existing aircraft engines and fueling infrastructure.

Today, Neste’s global SAF production capability is 1.5 million metric tons (around 515 million gallons) per annum, and it is set to grow to 2.2 million metric tons (around 750 million gallons) in 2027, when the expansion of Neste’s Rotterdam refinery is completed.

*) Neat, i.e. unblended, Neste MY Sustainable Aviation Fuel fulfills the mandatory sustainability criteria, including greenhouse gas emission reduction requirements over its life cycle compared to fossil fuel in accordance with e.g. ReFuelEU, CORSIA or RFS. While SAF and fossil jet fuel release similar amounts of CO2 during flight, SAF’s life cycle climate impact is smaller than fossil jet fuel’s. SAF can currently be blended up to 50% with conventional jet fuel.

Neste in brief

Neste (NESTE, Nasdaq Helsinki) is the world's leading producer of renewable diesel and sustainable aviation fuel (SAF), with production on three continents. Neste’s strategy focuses on growth in renewable fuels. The company’s renewables production capacity is expected to reach 6.8 million tons annually in 2027. Neste also produces high-quality oil products at its Porvoo refinery in Finland. The company has a network of nearly 1,000 fuel stations with expanding service offering, such as EV charging, in Finland and in the Baltics. Neste is included in many international indices for its sustainability performance. In 2025, Neste's revenue stood at EUR 19.0 billion. Read more: neste.com

text:
Global delivery giant FedEx announced a series of new agreements anticipated to secure more than 20 million gallons of neat sustainable aviation fuel (SAF) for use at five U.S. airports through 2027.

The new agreements mark an expansion of FedEx’s deployment of SAF across its U.S. air network, following deals in 2025 which secured approximately 5 million gallons of neat SAF resulting in the deployment of 16.5 million gallons of blended SAF at U.S. airports.

In 2021, FedEx announced a goal to achieve carbon neutrality in operations by 2040, allocating $2 billion in investments to reach its goal, with a focus on key areas including vehicle electrification, sustainable energy, and carbon sequestration. FedEx said that the new agreements align with its goal to source 30% of jet fuel blended from alternative sources by 2030.

The new agreements cover FedEx operations at Newark Liberty International Airport (EWR), Oakland International Airport (OAK), Miami International Airport (MIA), John F. Kennedy International Airport (JFK), and Dallas Fort Worth International Airport (DFW).

According to FedEx, through the next phase of procurement, SAF blends will represent a significant share of FedEx jet fuel use at the five airports. Blend ratios are expected to range from 30% to 50%, depending on location, the company said.

The company added that it will continue evaluating opportunities to expand SAF use where supply, infrastructure, and economics align with the needs of its air network.

Karen Blanks Ellis, Chief Sustainability Officer and Vice President of Environmental Affairs at FedEx, said:

“For the market to grow, supply needs to be reliable, affordable, and sustainable. Expanding our procurement allows us to employ more SAF in our network while bolstering the demand for greater production and scale.”

In 2025, United used over 83,000 metric tons (roughly 27.7 million gallons) of SAF, a 104% increase over the prior year, making it the largest SAF user among major U.S. airlines that year, based on publicly available reports, and expanded its SAF use to three additional hub airports in Newark, Washington D.C. and Houston, bringing the airlines’ SAF usage to six out of its seven domestic hubs. At Chicago O’Hare specifically, United was the first airline to purchase and use blended SAF in August 2024. O’Hare is United’s largest hub by daily departures and among the airline’s most important global gateways, making it a key location for scaling the use of blended SAF in day-to-day operations.

In Amsterdam, United has been using Neste MY SAF at Schiphol Airport since 2022. United was the first airline globally to use SAF in ongoing operations. Leveraging SAF and other measures to reduce GHG emissions, United is committed to reaching its net-zero emissions by 2050 goal.

“This extended agreement with United Airlines covering two international airports across two major aviation regions is a testament to our joint belief in the critical role of SAF in reducing aviation related GHG emissions*. By continuing to make SAF available at two of United’s key hubs, we are proving that SAF is a readily available, scalable solution, and we look forward to continuing our longstanding collaboration,” says Carl Nyberg, Senior Vice President, Commercial, Renewable Products business at Neste.

text:
The Government should price families out of flying by raising airfares by £600, a controversial climate quango has said.

The Climate Change Committee (CCC), which advises ministers, said on Wednesday that Labour should adopt a “polluter pays” model to force customers to bear the cost of Britain’s net zero push.

According to the CCC, lifting fares would make net zero easier to achieve by reducing demand for flights by 25pc and covering the expense of green jet fuel, known as sustainable aviation fuel (SAF), to help fund the transition away from kerosene.

It said the phased increase would amount to between 6p and 9p a mile by 2050, similar to the duty on petrol. This would add £150 to the cost of a return ticket to Alicante – £600 for a family of four – or £400 for an individual return flight to New York.

The CCC recommendation was prompted by Heathrow’s plans to build a third runway. It said fare increases should be enshrined in law before ministers grant permission for the runway, which is aiming to be approved by 2029.

Nigel Topping, the CCC’s chairman, said the committee had been invited by ministers to provide advice on the draft blueprint for the Heathrow runway.

He said: “Our key conclusion is that the Government cannot expand Heathrow Airport without requiring the aviation industry to clean up its emissions.

“Emissions from flying are projected to rise even without Heathrow expansion and the UK does not currently have a credible plan to bring them down.

“Government needs to ensure that the aviation industry takes responsibility for the emissions it creates and bears the costs of decarbonisation. Those conditions do not exist today.”

He said the summer heatwaves had “brought the impacts of climate change into sharp focus” and that every ton of greenhouse gas emissions “makes those impacts worse”.

The CCC said penalising travellers was not unreasonable because half of people in England do not fly abroad and the most affluent 20pc take almost two fifths of flights.

‘Turning the clock back’

By 2050, it said, the successful shift of other industries away from fossil fuels will mean aviation accounts for “almost all” UK carbon emissions.

The emissions from the £49bn expansion of Heathrow alone will be larger than for any other sector of the economy, it said.

Tim Alderslade, the head of the Airlines UK lobby group, said the recommendations risked “turning the clock back to a time when flying was the preserve of the rich”.

He said: “You can’t solve the climate crisis by pricing Britain out of the skies. The CCC’s approach would add £600 to a family’s trip to Europe and £1,600 to New York, putting holidays out of reach for millions.

“The transition has to be affordable. Airlines are already investing billions in new aircraft, SAF and airspace upgrades and we have a plan to deliver it.”

Tania Kumar, of the Confederation of British Industry, said Britain needed to “move beyond the false choice between economic growth and environmental progress” and focus on airspace reform, scaling up SAF production and commercialising carbon removal technologies.

Heathrow said passengers already paid billions of pounds in carbon taxes and that a growing aviation sector could deliver “huge economic and social value” to Britain.

According to the CCC, passing on costs to depress demand would deliver 24pc of the reduction in emissions needed to hit net zero by 2050.

A fifth would come from efficiency improvements and a further 20pc would be met by switching to SAF. A further 36pc would be delivered by so-called engineered removals, such as carbon capture.

With a similar goal, it also vows to step up the planning and cooperation for 6G network in the Greater Bay Area and the upgrading of new communications infrastructure, in support of the digital transformation of various industries.

In a move to facilitate the movement of people and goods, both crucial manufacturing resources, the government said it strives to extend the operating hours of land border crossings with Shenzhen, enabling passengers and cargo from the Greater Bay Area to connect with global markets via Hong Kong in a more convenient way.

To accelerate innovation, Hong Kong itself will also seek to attract leading innovation and technology talent from around the world, along with their businesses, investments and research achievements. Released on the same day, the latest Policy Address adds more specific measures to advance cooperation with Guangdong next year. Hong Kong will work to establish a sustainable aviation fuel production base in Dongguan, combining their technological and industrial strengths to build a green industry chain with global influence.

The city will also collaborate with Guangdong to advance new industrialization, and team up with Shenzhen to promote the establishment of industrial innovation platforms and mechanisms to boost industry chain synergy for emerging and future industries.

Gordon Kee, a research associate of the Hong Kong Institute of Asia-Pacific Studies at the Chinese University of Hong Kong, noted that developing innovation and technology is not only a national strategy but also a key priority for Hong Kong at present.

“Strengthening cooperation with mainland cities in the Greater Bay Area —particularly Shenzhen — will help generate greater synergies, make more effective use of resources, and accelerate the commercialization of research outcomes, while avoiding the possibility of disorderly or even malicious competition between the two sides,” he said.

“While significant progress has been made in cross-boundary infrastructure and mechanism connectivity, numerous bottlenecks remain. Hong Kong’s first five-year plan can be seen as a commitment to remove these obstacles that hinder deeper regional integration.”

In many areas of high-tech industrial cooperation mentioned in the plan — such as hydrogen energy and 6G — Hong Kong can fully leverage its strengths to establish industry standards aligned with international norms and effectively integrate them with the mainland’s robust industrial foundation, Kee believes.

Fan Kwok-yuen, assistant professor in the Department of Economics and Finance at The Hang Seng University of Hong Kong, noted that these new initiatives are concrete demonstrations of the ideal Shenzhen–Hong Kong cooperation model that proposes to leverage the two sides’ complementary strengths in high-end research and development, advanced manufacturing, and modern services.

He noted that cooperation in emerging industries can help Hong Kong integrate more closely into the Greater Bay Area’s innovation and manufacturing networks, yet deep industrial synergy cannot be achieved through project lists alone. Enhancing connectivity and strengthening mutual recognition of standards are tasks that must be pursued consistently over the next five years.

title: Understanding Chemical Oxygen Demand in Wastewater - AZoCleantech
description:
Chemical oxygen demand (COD) indicates the amount of oxygen required to oxidize organic matter in a body of water.

text:
Chemical oxygen demand (COD) indicates the amount of oxygen required to oxidize organic matter in a body of water. It can therefore be used to assess how potentially polluting an effluent may be when released into the natural environment.

Discharging effluent with a high COD can lower dissolved oxygen levels in the receiving environment. This reduction may damage local ecosystems, including the organisms and biological communities that depend on them. As environmental regulations become increasingly stringent, COD is monitored to confirm that effluent discharge will not adversely affect nearby ecosystems.

How Is COD Measured in Wastewater?

Several techniques are available for determining COD in wastewater. These include colorimetric analysis with dichromate reagents, closed reflux methods, and approaches based on the time required to digest organic compounds.

However, operators often encounter difficulties because these methods are not only complicated but also expensive. They also generally do not allow COD to be monitored continuously or in real time.

Can UV254 Be Used to Estimate or Replace COD?

A more straightforward and cost-effective approach is to estimate COD through a surrogate parameter, such as UV254 absorbance.

What Is the Relationship or Correlation Between UV254 and COD?

The absorbance measured at a particular wavelength is related to the concentration of organic compounds that absorb light at that wavelength. Wavelengths around 254 nm are especially useful because many organic substances absorb ultraviolet light in this region.

Because UV254 absorbance generally increases with the concentration of organic matter, a linear correlation between UV254 and COD can often be developed. UV254 can then serve as a surrogate for COD, provided that the types of organic compounds contributing to the absorbance remain reasonably consistent.

It is important to recognize that UV254 absorbance does not necessarily correlate with all water quality parameters. A correlation may be absent when the relevant parameter in a particular water source is associated with substances that do not absorb UV254 light.

For example, a water supply containing a substantial amount of dissolved sugar could have a high COD, even though sugar does not absorb UV254.

Correlation study between COD and UV254 absorbance on industrial wastewater. Image Credit: Process Instruments (UK)

The data above come from a correlation study comparing COD with UV254 absorbance in industrial wastewater samples. The results provide a visual illustration of the relationship between COD and UV254 absorbance.

How Can a UV254 Sensor be used to Measure COD?

The UV254Sense probe from Pi uses a high-quality, long-life UV LED that produces light at a wavelength of 254 nm. The light passes through a sapphire window and travels through the water sample before reaching a photodiode detector on the opposite side.

The proportion of light lost through absorption is referred to as UVA. Since absorbance is the measurement of interest, the UVA value can be used to establish a correlation factor and produce a surrogate estimate of COD.

UV254Sense Probe. Image Credit: Process Instruments (UK)

UV254 COD Correlation Example: Wastewater and Water

Pi’s service engineers recently upgraded a UV254 COD monitoring system at a wastewater treatment works in Türkiye. The facility uses Pi’s UV254 COD monitoring technology to help ensure that its effluent discharge into a nearby river remains below the legal limit of 5 mg/L.

The system has operated reliably and continuously for more than six years.

Pi’s UV254 COD monitoring system. Image Credit: Process Instruments (UK)

What Is a “Good” UV254 Probe?

Pi’s new UV254Sense probe is designed to offer advantages over other UV probes on the market. It is relatively simple to operate and maintain because it contains no moving parts. Furthermore, its running costs are also comparatively low, as the system does not require reagents.

Further information is available about using UV254 as a surrogate for other measurements, including total organic carbon (TOC) and biological oxygen demand (BOD).

This information has been sourced, reviewed, and adapted from materials provided by Process Instruments (UK).

text:
South Africa’s Phelan Green Hydrogen has taken final investment decision (FID) on the first phase of its green hydrogen-based sustainable aviation fuel (e-SAF) project.

It came as the country’s president revealed the “first wave” of projects backed by its green hydrogen programme.

The six projects, led by Phelan’s 140,000 tonne-per-year facility in the Western Cape, gained backing following President Ramaphosa’s attendance at the 18th BRICS summit, where leaders agreed to cooperate on hydrogen and its value chains.

Phelan’s e-SAF facility is the furthest advanced of the projects. Following $100m in Phelan investment, it is due to begin construction early next year and, according to Ramaphosa, could export fuel by the first quarter of 2029.

The remaining five projects comprise a spread of technologies at different points in the development pathway.

Enertrag and ArcelorMittal’s Saldanha hydrogen-based direct reduced iron (DRI) project and Green e-Fuels Producers’ green methanol infrastructure corridor both sit at the pre-feasibility stage.

Hive Hydrogen’s Coega green ammonia project was identified as having completed early preparatory work, and the Prieska Power Reserve green ammonia project is in the development stage. Both are planned to come online by 2030.

Further advanced is a small-scale project by Green Hydrogen Solutions, aimed at domestic demand, which has completed front-end engineering design studies.

Ramaphosa stopped short of solidifying fiscal support for the projects, but said the wave would concentrate on “project preparation, investment mobilisation and government coordination,” to assist in achieving FIDs

He also said a second wave of projects would follow.

South Africa appears to move in tow with the BRICS nations, the most prominent of whom have all displayed strong signals in the hydrogen space.

India, which hosted the summit, was recently identified alongside fellow attendee China as leading global hydrogen momentum, by CEOs surveyed in the Hydrogen Council’s Global Hydrogen Compass 2026.

South Africa is regarded as a promising region for exporting green hydrogen and derivatives, benefiting from abundant wind and solar resources, established industrial infrastructure, and access to platinum group metals used in electrolysers and fuel cells.

FedEx is expanding its sustainable aviation fuel (SAF) procurement through new agreements expected to secure more than 20 million gallons of neat SAF across five US airports through 2027.

The agreements cover FedEx operations at Newark Liberty International Airport, Oakland International Airport, Miami International Airport, John F. Kennedy International Airport and Dallas Fort Worth International Airport. SAF will be supplied at blend ratios ranging from 30% to 50%, depending on the location.

The procurement forms part of FedEx’s target to source 30% of its jet fuel from blended alternative sources by 2030 and expand SAF use across its US air network.

“The latest agreements represent an expansion of SAF within the FedEx air network enabled, in part, by state and federal level incentives,” said Greg Paulus, Vice President of Enterprise Sourcing.

Since 2025, FedEx has secured approximately 5 million gallons of neat SAF through agreements that have supported the deployment of 16.5 million gallons of blended SAF across five US airports.

Under the latest agreements, SAF blends are expected to account for a significant share of FedEx’s jet fuel consumption at the five airports.

Karen Blanks Ellis, chief sustainability officer and vice president of Environmental Affairs at FedEx, said, “SAF is one of the most impactful decarbonization solutions available to aviation today and an important part of our approach to reducing emissions. For the market to grow, supply needs to be reliable, affordable, and sustainable. Expanding our procurement allows us to employ more SAF in our network while bolstering the demand for greater production and scale.”

The new agreements will further expand SAF use across the FedEx network, reflecting growing demand. As the market develops, FedEx will continue to explore opportunities to increase SAF adoption where supply, infrastructure and economics support its air network needs.

title: Emerson selected to automate new SAF facility under construction
description:
Emerson has been awarded a contract by Technip Energies to provide automation technologies for the SkyNRG sustainable aviation fuel (SAF) plant—the first dedicated greenfield SAF production facility in Europe.
Currently under construction in Delfzijl, the new SAF facility will support the Netherlands' efforts to meet the EU's sustainable aviation fuel mandate.
Once fully operational in 2028, the facility is expected to produce approximately 100,000 tonnes of SAF annually.
“Developing Europe’s first dedicated sustainable aviation fuel facility is a major step in scaling SAF production and supporting aviation decarbonisation,” said Bart Rosendaal, site director of DSL-01 at SkyNRG.
“Projects such as SkyNRG’s SAF facility represent the future of energy and sustainable fuels,” said Nathan Pettus, president of Emerson’s process systems and solutions business.
text:
Emerson has been awarded a contract by Technip Energies to provide automation technologies for the SkyNRG sustainable aviation fuel (SAF) plant—the first dedicated greenfield SAF production facility in Europe.

Emerson’s DeltaV™ integrated control and safety system (ICSS) will help ensure safe, reliable startup and long-term operational performance, while reducing project risk for this first-of-its-kind facility.

Currently under construction in Delfzijl, the new SAF facility will support the Netherlands' efforts to meet the EU's sustainable aviation fuel mandate.

Once fully operational in 2028, the facility is expected to produce approximately 100,000 tonnes of SAF annually.

The plant will convert residual fats and greases into a sustainable “drop-in” fuel that can be blended with conventional jet fuel without requiring modifications to aircraft or fuelling infrastructure.

The project will also support compliance with the ReFuelEU Aviation Regulation, which requires all jet fuel supplied at EU airports to contain a minimum of 2% SAF from 2025, rising to 70% by 2050.

“Developing Europe’s first dedicated sustainable aviation fuel facility is a major step in scaling SAF production and supporting aviation decarbonisation,” said Bart Rosendaal, site director of DSL-01 at SkyNRG.

“Working with experienced partners like Technip Energies and Emerson helps ensure we can deliver a safe, reliable and future-ready plant from day one.”

As a greenfield facility, the plant will be born digital, with advanced automation technologies implemented from the outset to ensure efficient, reliable and safe operations. The ICSS will include Emerson’s DeltaV Distributed Control System and DeltaV Safety Instrumented System, providing process control, safety shutdown and fire and gas detection.

Emerson’s AMS Device Manager plant asset management software will support efficient commissioning and ongoing maintenance by delivering device data, health insights and advanced diagnostics from intelligent field devices.

These systems will manage all process units, including the hydroprocessed esters and fatty acids process to produce SAF, an advanced feedstock pre-treatment unit and an on-site hydrogen plant based on Technip Energies’ proprietary high efficiency steam methane reforming technology.

“Projects such as SkyNRG’s SAF facility represent the future of energy and sustainable fuels,” said Nathan Pettus, president of Emerson’s process systems and solutions business. “With complex, first-of-a-kind plants, early engineering alignment and a fully integrated automation architecture are key to delivering predictable project outcomes and consistent operational performance over the long term.”

title: Heathrow's third runway should only be approved if emissions are reduced, report advises
description:
The third runway at Heathrow should not be approved unless the aviation industry commits to reducing carbon dioxide emissions, project advisers have said.
"This is the only way that the proposed Heathrow expansion could be considered consistent with the UK's carbon budgets and net zero," the report said.
However, the report notes that if the industry pays for sustainable aviation fuels and removal of emissions, this will likely be passed on to ticket prices.
Heathrow is currently responsible for around half of aviation emissions in Britain.
"We will carefully consider CCC's advice along with all responses received to the Heathrow expansion consultation."
text:
The third runway at Heathrow should not be approved unless the aviation industry commits to reducing carbon dioxide emissions, project advisers have said.

A report by the Climate Change Committee (CCC), an independent body established under 2008's Climate Change Act, stated that the expansion would only be permissible if airlines commit to greener fuel.

The CCC laid out ways that the industry could reduce emissions by 2050, such as through the government requiring the industry to pay the costs of decarbonisation and investing in sustainable aviation fuel.

The group also recommended engineered removal machines, which capture carbon dioxide from the atmosphere and store it permanently.

"This is the only way that the proposed Heathrow expansion could be considered consistent with the UK's carbon budgets and net zero," the report said.

However, the report notes that if the industry pays for sustainable aviation fuels and removal of emissions, this will likely be passed on to ticket prices.

It estimates that ticket prices could increase by around £150 for a return trip to Alicante and £400 for a return trip to New York by 2050, around six to nine pence per mile, similar to fuel duty on petrol and diesel today.

The report also points out that while sustainable aviation fuel and engineered removals are viable, it is uncertain if they can be deployed on a mass scale within the net zero timeline.

While the government has made investment plans in this area, further action would need to be taken to use them in the long term.

The CCC says that emissions from aviation have more than doubled since 1990, while industries that make up the rest of the economy have halved theirs.

Even if the third runway did not go ahead, the advisers say that under the current policies, emissions would not fall at all by 2050. Heathrow is currently responsible for around half of aviation emissions in Britain.

It predicts the expansion would only make it harder for the UK to meet its climate targets and forecasts that the full impact of the expansion would account for 6.9 per cent of the country's remaining carbon emissions by 2050.

A Heathrow spokesperson says that its expansion cannot be a choice between economic growth and meeting the UK's net zero targets – "it must deliver both".

"The CCC's assessment does not change this and acknowledges that the key solutions exist today," they continued.

"We will continue working with government and partners across the aviation sector to ramp up today's proven technologies, while examining options for how the billions of pounds passengers already pay in carbon taxes can be used to support this.

"Given the right policies, a growing aviation sector can be empowered to deliver the huge economic and social value that air travel brings, while increasing pace of delivery of the solutions needed to accelerate aviation's decarbonisation."

The DfT said that "any expansion proposal would need to align with our net zero targets".

"We're investing £219 million in sustainable aviation fuel production and a further £43 million in cleaner technologies to support greener aviation, while expansion could deliver around £40 billion to the economy and support up to 60,000 local jobs.

"We will carefully consider CCC's advice along with all responses received to the Heathrow expansion consultation."

title: Africa's largest refinery fills Europe's fuel gap as first-half profit reaches $1.82 billion
description:
The figures were reported by Reuters⁠ as Dangote Petroleum Refinery seeks investors for Africa’s largest initial public offering.
A dramatic financial turnaround The refinery recorded revenue of more than $13 billion and a net profit of $1.82 billion during the first half of 2026.
ADVERTISEMENT Dangote also increased diesel and gasoil exports to Europe and West Africa as buyers competed for available supplies.
Middle Eastern disruptions have reduced European supplies, while wars and attacks on refineries have tightened the global diesel market.
If those supplies recover, European fuel prices and refining margins could fall.
text:
The Nigerian refinery exported about 80,000 barrels of jet fuel daily to Europe during the quarter, making it the region’s largest external supplier after the United States.

The figures were reported by Reuters⁠ as Dangote Petroleum Refinery seeks investors for Africa’s largest initial public offering.

Middle Eastern disruptions removed about one-quarter of Europe’s normal diesel and jet-fuel supplies and pushed regional inventories to their lowest level in 12 years.

ADVERTISEMENT

Dangote’s ability to increase exports during the shortage gave the refinery an unusually valuable position in Europe’s aviation-fuel market less than two years after it began production.

A dramatic financial turnaround

The refinery recorded revenue of more than $13 billion and a net profit of $1.82 billion during the first half of 2026. That compares with a $476 million loss in 2025, when the facility was still increasing production and carrying substantial financing costs.

Pulse Nigeria

Its earnings were supported by rising output and the widening difference between the price of crude oil and the amount refiners could charge for diesel and jet fuel.

ADVERTISEMENT

Dangote also increased diesel and gasoil exports to Europe and West Africa as buyers competed for available supplies.

The refinery’s location on Nigeria’s Atlantic coast gives it direct access to European and American markets without requiring ships to travel through the Strait of Hormuz or the Red Sea.

That position has become increasingly valuable as attacks and shipping restrictions disrupt fuel flows from the Middle East.

The development also gives investors a clearer picture of the export business supporting the refinery’s proposed valuation of approximately $47 billion to $49 billion.

Dangote is offering 4.1 billion new shares at N525 each in an IPO expected to raise approximately $1.6 billion (N2.15 trillion). The proceeds will partly finance a planned expansion that would double processing capacity to 1.4 million barrels daily.

ADVERTISEMENT

The company is also considering a secondary listing in the United States within four years⁠.

The risk behind the opportunity

The supply crisis supports Dangote’s profit and valuation case, but it also creates an important risk for prospective investors.

Current fuel margins reflect extraordinary market conditions. Middle Eastern disruptions have reduced European supplies, while wars and attacks on refineries have tightened the global diesel market.

If those supplies recover, European fuel prices and refining margins could fall. Dangote would then have to rely more heavily on efficiency, stable crude supplies and sustained demand rather than scarcity-driven prices.

ADVERTISEMENT

The refinery’s ability to produce different fuels and process as many as 36 crude grades gives it flexibility. Its size also provides economies unavailable to many older European refineries.

However, investors must weigh those advantages against the cost and execution risk of the planned $14.3 billion expansion, possible regulatory changes in Nigeria and the volatility of global fuel markets.

Dangote’s European exports show that the refinery has moved beyond replacing Nigeria’s imports. It is becoming an important supplier to one of the world’s biggest fuel markets. The larger question is whether it can maintain that position after the present shortage ends.

text:
South African energy and chemicals group Sasol has signed an agreement to supply sustainable aviation fuel to White Desert, a luxury-tourism company that operates flights between Cape Town and Antarctica.

The agreement represents Sasol’s first commercial supply of the fuel, according to a company statement published on 15 September⁠.

The first flight using the South African-made fuel is expected to depart in November aboard an Airbus A340-600, Reuters reported⁠.

ADVERTISEMENT

White Desert operates approximately one flight weekly during Antarctica’s November-to-February tourism season. Its packages range from a $16,500 one-day visit to seven-day expeditions costing as much as $120,000.

DON'T MISS THIS: Africa’s largest economy boosts fuel production as 108,000 bpd refinery returns online

The company’s guests can visit emperor penguin colonies, explore glaciers and stay in heated camps on the continent. The new agreement connects that high-end tourism market with South Africa’s emerging cleaner-fuel industry.

From European imports to South African fuel

White Desert has used sustainable aviation fuel since 2021 but previously sourced it from Europe. It is switching to Sasol after the South African company secured international sustainability certification for fuel produced at its Natref refinery.

ADVERTISEMENT

Natref, located in Sasolburg, has the capacity to process approximately 108,500 barrels daily. It is also South Africa’s only inland crude-oil refinery⁠.

BI Africa

Sasol’s product is made by processing renewable materials, including used cooking and vegetable oils, alongside conventional feedstock. It can be used in existing aircraft after being blended with ordinary jet fuel, avoiding the need to replace engines or build new airport-fuelling systems.

DON'T MISS THIS:See inside the former Emirates Airbus A340 that flies passengers to Antarctica by landing on a runway made of ice

The arrangement gives Sasol a named commercial customer months after Natref received certification from Germany’s TÜV SÜD. The certification also opened a possible route into Europe, where airlines face progressively higher requirements to use sustainable fuel.

ADVERTISEMENT

Sasol has said Natref could produce approximately 100 million litres of sustainable aviation fuel annually by 2030. Combined with planned production at its Secunda complex, that figure could reach 200 million litres.

Cleaner, but not emission-free

The agreement does not mean the aircraft will fly entirely on recycled cooking oil or operate without emissions.

Sustainable aviation fuel is normally blended with conventional fuel, and aircraft still release carbon dioxide when it is burned. Its environmental advantage comes largely from reusing renewable waste instead of extracting additional crude oil.

White Desert says sustainable fuels can reduce lifecycle emissions substantially compared with conventional jet fuel. However, the actual reduction depends on the feedstock, manufacturing process and amount blended into the aircraft’s fuel.

ADVERTISEMENT

Neither company disclosed the volume covered by the agreement, its financial value or the renewable portion of the final blend. Those details will determine the project’s real commercial and environmental importance.

Still, the deal moves South Africa’s sustainable aviation ambitions beyond certification and into commercial use, with one of the world’s most remote and expensive flight routes serving as its first showcase.

title: Airbus' Route to a Sustainable Aerospace Future
description:
